brief: The town has been telling you about barges for a hundred iterations — 'A barge horn sounds somewhere far downstream' is one of the ticker's deliberately unplaced SOUNDS — and the river has never carried one. Meanwhile the quay is a walkway, not a wharf: x112..114, a rail at 112.9, two benches, no steps to the water, nothing ever tied up. Bring a barge up the west channel on some days and let it work the quay. The water is clear for it: the eyot hugs the EAST channel (124.3, rx 1.75) and the punt lives off JETTY 128.4, so a hull around x 115-118 meets nothing, and the footbridge (DECK rows 30..32, PARAPET_Z 1.0) is the southern limit — the reach north of it is the barge's water. Model it on the punt: a hull that owns its own tick and its own schedule, never a share of laneCap. Then give the horn a subject — sayAt at the quay — so a sound the town has always made finally has somewhere to come from.
successLooksLike: On a barge day the wide shot shows a long hull come down the west channel, tie alongside the quay, sit being worked for a stretch of the day and go; the horn is said with a SUBJECT at the quay instead of nowhere; and `structures` moves in the census (the moorings counted in __census()'s structure block), with the baseline re-pinned and said so.
avoid: Not a second ferry — the punt was worked at #128 and #131 and another passenger hull is c208's brief, not this one. Do not route it under the footbridge. Do not spend its people out of laneCap or eastCap; a rare thing needs its own source.
